subject: Elastic reserve runway + surge policy proposal for Clover Labs Dedicated
messages:
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.inference.com>
To: Evan Wells <evan.wells@cloverlabs.com>, Nicole Tran <nicole.tran@cloverlabs.com>
Cc: 
Date: Mon, 10 Jun 2029 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: Elastic reserve runway + surge policy for Dedicated capacity

Hi Evan / Nicole,

Thanks again for the walkthrough today — excited to get Clover Labs onto a Dedicated pool. To help us size the Dedicated slab and design a surge/autoscale policy that matches your product peaks, could you confirm the following by end of week?

- Typical sustained concurrency (peak 95th percentile requests/min) across your inference endpoints.
- Expected token generation distribution (median vs 95th token length).
- Ratio of high-priority (interactive UI) vs background batch/async traffic.
- Any calendar-based bursts (daily launch windows, weekly reports, marketing pushes).

Our initial thoughts: allocate a pre-warmed reserve of N GPUs (we'll fill that in after numbers) plus an "elastic reserve runway" — a transient burst pool that can be claimed for up to X minutes before billing/grace credits apply. This avoids cold-starts while letting us keep committed capacity reasonable.

I've attached the request summary we discussed. Once you share the workload sample (a small CSV or telemetry snapshot) I'll loop in Marcus and Ben to produce a suggested fleet plan and a draft autoscale policy with concrete parameters (ramp windows, cooldown/hysteresis, eviction priority, and pre-warm thresholds).

Proposed next steps:
1) You send sample_workload.csv (or a telemetry export).
2) We provide a 1-page surge runway sizing and a Day-0 ops checklist.
3) If that looks good, we include the surge runway terms in the Dedicated amendment and schedule a runbook review.

Fyi — because Clover expects sub-200ms p99s for UI flows, we'll plan for a short tail-latency buffer and aggressive prefix caching.

Thanks,

Lauren Bishop
Account Lead, Redwood Inference
lauren.bishop@redwood.inference.com
Redwood Inference

Attachment: clover_request_summary.pdf (1 page)

From: Evan Wells <evan.wells@cloverlabs.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.inference.com>
Cc: Nicole Tran <nicole.tran@cloverlabs.com>
Date: Tue, 11 Jun 2029 10:34:15 -0700
Subject: Re: Elastic reserve runway + surge policy for Dedicated capacity

Hi Lauren,

Thanks — attached a small extract from our last 30 days (sample_workload.csv). Key points:
- 95th requests/min: ~1,800 across our two main endpoints (embed + chat).
- Median token gen: 120 tokens; 95th token gen: 780 tokens (longer analytic queries).
- Traffic mix: ~65% interactive, 35% background. Background jobs spike nightly 02:00-03:00 PT with heavy batches.
- We run marketing-driven spikes (email campaigns) roughly twice a month that can multiply interactive traffic by 2.5x for ~20 minutes.

SLA: We are targeting p99 < 250ms for interactive flows where possible; willing to accept slightly higher p99 during the known campaign spikes if the autoscale can reclaim capacity quickly.

Let us know what you recommend. Also, we have a procurement cycle that prefers a small runway of committed GPUs plus surge credits rather than a large flat reservation.

Cheers,
Evan

Attachment: sample_workload.csv

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.inference.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.inference.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.inference.com>
Cc: 
Date: Wed, 12 Jun 2029 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Elastic reserve runway + surge policy for Dedicated capacity

Marcus / Ben — forwarding Clover's telemetry extract (below). Their preferences: small committed slab + surge credits / runway. They care about p99 for interactive flows and have predictable nightly batches + twice-monthly marketing spikes.

Ask: can you two draft a Fleet & Autoscale proposal that includes:
- A recommended committed GPU slab and a transient burst pool size (in GPUs) for immediate pre-warm claiming.
- Surge runway definition: max duration (minutes), grace credits behaviour, and billing implications.
- Eviction & priority rules (how background batch is preempted vs interactive).
- Cooldown/hysteresis settings to avoid oscillation during the 20-min campaign spikes.
- Suggested SLA addendum language for p99 and compensation for extended surge events.

Also include a short ops playbook (on-call steps when surge > runway, fallback to hosted model variants, runbook link).

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.inference.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.inference.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.inference.com>
Cc: 
Date: Thu, 13 Jun 2029 14:02:58 -0700
Subject: Re: Elastic reserve runway + surge policy for Dedicated capacity — Fleet & Policy draft

Team — draft below (attached spreadsheet with sizing calculations). Happy to iterate.

Attachment: fleet_plan_v1.xlsx, autoscale_policy_draft.md

Executive summary:
- Recommended committed slab: 24 A100-equivalent GPUs (balanced to handle base 95th load with caching).
- Elastic reserve (burst runway): 8 GPUs pre-warmed, available for bursts up to 30 minutes per event. After 30 minutes, surge credits begin to apply at the agreed transient rate unless the customer converts to a short-term commit.
- Eviction & priority: interactive requests are tagged with higher priority. When reserve is exhausted, background batch capacity is throttled first with graceful draining (20s TTL) to free headroom.
- Scale mechanics:
  - Scale-up trigger: sustained 10% over committed CPU/GPU utilization for 60s (to avoid reacting to single noisy spikes).
  - Pre-warm trigger: predictive pre-warm when marketing campaign flag is set (API + scheduled window).
  - Scale-down: hysteresis of 5 minutes after utilization falls below 50% to prevent oscillation during 20-minute campaign spikes.
- Billing & credits: 30-minute free runway per distinct spike, then transient billing at 1.8x committed rate. We recommend offering Clover an initial 3 free runway events per quarter as a concession.
- SLA addendum: p99 target 250ms for interactive flows during steady state; during runway-triggered bursts, p99 target relaxed to 450ms for up to 30 minutes before remediation credits apply.

Operational notes:
- Canary window: first 2 weeks after go-live we'll enable a conservative autoscaler (longer ramp) and monitor telemetry; if p99 consistently < 250ms, we tighten cooldowns.
- Fallback: automatic downgrade to compact model variants (quantized) if sustained runway exhaustion > 45 minutes, with notification to Clover and optional manual override.
- Runbook: link to runbook + escalation contacts included in the spreadsheet.

Requesting approval on the following items to push to procurement: committed slab size, burst runway length (30m), and the 3-event quarterly concession. Also confirm whether they want surge billing invoiced monthly or reconciled at quarter end.

— Ben
Senior Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.inference.com

From: Evan Wells <evan.wells@cloverlabs.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.inference.com>
Cc: Nicole Tran <nicole.tran@cloverlabs.com>
Date: Fri, 14 Jun 2029 09:03:12 -0700
Subject: Re: Elastic reserve runway + surge policy for Dedicated capacity — Fleet & Policy draft

Hi Lauren / Ben,

This looks good and pragmatic — very aligned with procurement's preference. We accept the proposed committed slab (24 GPUs) and the 8-GPU, 30-minute elastic runway. The concession of 3 free runway events per quarter is appreciated.

Two asks before we sign:
1) Can you include explicit language around priority preemption (ensure background batch throttle happens within 60s of runway consumption)?
2) Please add a single-page ops checklist for the on-call engineer with exact Playbook steps for a runway breach.

If you can add those pieces and send the amended attachment + DocuSign link, we can get procurement moving.

Happy to schedule a 30-min runbook review next week.

Thanks,
Evan

DocuSign request: please send once amended.
